scope: Read-only CPU analysis of JSON/log metadata; no model loading, forward, GPU, training, code edits, FP16 export, or validation execution. Only this ignored JSON artifact is written.

metric_scope.precision: native training-validation metrics; reported as BF16 in task context; not actual deployment FP16 results

findings: 030 completes 13 epochs; best epoch8 and five subsequent non-improving epochs match patience5.
030 versus 029 native best: +0.003392853853 MacroAUC, six class AUC increases and four decreases. Point improvement does not establish statistical significance or diversity.
Late validation loss and training loss continue to decrease while MacroAUC drops. This supports objective/ranking divergence and class-specific deterioration, not numerical collapse.
Epoch8 to13 seven class AUCs rise while classes1,4,10 fall. Class1 drop dominates the macro decline; avoid claiming uniform class overfitting.
Training soft KL reaches its minimum at epoch9, then rises through epoch13; this indicates increasing divergence from the fixed teacher target, not evidence that changing alpha would help.

029 and 030 share the same resolution, initialization source, teacher cache, objective, schedule, and preprocessing; only seed/output differ in config. Seed diversity may help, but ensemble quality cannot be inferred from marginal AUCs.
limitations: No complete 030 per-Study valid probability archive is provided by history/config/best_metrics or the run top-level files. Paired patient-cluster confidence intervals, ensemble metrics, paired errors and subgroup/slice analysis cannot be computed from aggregate AUCs.

Do not compare the previous actual-FP16 mixed Tiny512+Tiny768 AUC 0.807157435 against current native-BF16 0.807569817 as a precise superiority test. Different precision and compositions require common deployed inference metrics and paired predictions.
Single official valid and its checkpoint selection introduce selection uncertainty. Neither significant seed gain nor guaranteed ensemble gain is established.
